item.title: Tim Maia - Disco Club
item.description: Label: Mr Bongo | Prix: 34,00 €
item.content:encoded:
Label: Mr Bongo

Prix: 34,00 €

Mr Bongo brings another Brazilian rarity to the masses with this sublime reissue of Tim Maia's Disco Club. Recorded in 1978, it's a latter-period gem from the larger than life legend, combining the glitz and glamour of disco's heyday with Maia's raw funk and soul roots.When Maia first heard Little Richard as a teenager, he knew what kind of singer and artist he wanted to be. Five formative years spent in the US, where he ran wild in NYC and joined adoo-wop group called the Ideals, did little to dampen his enthusiasm for black music.Stirred by the civil rights movement in the US and driven by a punk spirit, Maia went on to blaze his own trail through the early 70s over the course of four successful albums for Polydor. Moving away from the straight MPB, Tropicalia and international rock dominating the airwaves, his sound represented a new black Brazilian consciousness. When he sang, he could be raspy and defiant one moment ... and then romantic and reflective the next. But always on a groove and with a hook. It was an irresistible combination.Yet by 1977 he was bankrupt and in limbo having first joined a religious cult called Superior National and then alienated listeners with his first album sung entirely in English. To complicate matters further, Brazil was feeling the Saturday Night Fever. Gloria Gaynor, Chic and Kool & the Gang were dominating the charts and filling hotspots such as New York City Discotheque in Ipanema and Frenetic Dancing Days in the Gávea Mall.Maia left his usual band and went into the legendary Estudios Level with a mighty ensemble of Rio's finest including Paulinha Braga on drums, Jamil Joanes on bass, Robson Jorge on clarinet, Hyldon De Souza on guitar, Sidinho on percussion, trombonists Edmundo Maciel and Darcy Seixas, and Juarez Assis on tenor sax.Arranger and keyboardist Lincoln Olivetti was a crucial presence during these sessions. He added that all-important string flourish and brassy joy to the uptempo tracks while giving thestar enough room to express himself. The album kicks off with a trio of floor fillers: the exuberant party starter 'A Fim De Voltar', a sing-a-long anthem in 'Acenda O Farol' and the undeniably funky hit 'Sossego' (file that one next to Fatback).But then Maia drops it down and gets existential on 'All I Want', questioning the meaning of happiness. He also shows his tender side on slow burners such as 'Murmúrio' (written by the great Cassiano) and 'Pais E Filhos', the latter featuring a supersoft bed of harmonies you can't help but lay down on. But the party ain't over and mid-tempo groover 'Juras' gets the feet moving again before 'Jhony' sends us swaying off into the night.Maia's appetite for excess would eventually get the better of him. But Disco Club is the sound of an unpredictable genius on top form. Get ready for the time of your life.

House MasterpieceSome 30 years after they first met in the DJ booth of Tokyo’s Spacelab Yellow nightclub, close friends François Kevorkian and Dimitri From Paris have finally joined forces in the studio. The result is The Nassau Excursion, a dazzlingly good three-track EP inspired by their joint love of disco and boogie-era dance records made at Island Records’ Compass Point Studio in the Bahamas. Across three essential tracks, François and Dimitri explore and celebrate this distinctive Caribbean post-disco sound – one where weighty basslines and heavy drum machine beats rub shoulders with early ‘80s synths, dub-style production, heady hand percussion patterns and arrangements drenched in space echo and tape delay.[info sheet from distr.]

item.title: Tom Carruthers - Neutralise EP
item.description: Label: Wax Classic | Prix: 14,00 € | Style: House, Chicago House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Wax Classic

Prix: 14,00 €

Style: House, Chicago House

UK producer Tom Carruthers returns with a scorching 5-tracker for Skylax Records, diving headfirst into the primal roots of jackin’ house, proto-italo, and early machine funk. Known for his raw MPC-driven grooves on L.I.E.S., Clone Jack For Daze, Syncrophone, and Craigie Knowes, Carruthers channels the energy of the underground circa ’86—pure drum machine soul for the dancefloor faithful. Side A kicks off with the title track “Neutralise”, all sharp snares, warped synths and hypnotic repetition—a jack track in the truest sense. “Deep North” follows with ghostly pads and relentless drum programming, while “No More” brings metallic tension and stripped-down funk with a heavy nod to Chicago’s original blueprints. On the flip, “Pascals” weaves cosmic arps through rugged percussion, merging italo sensuality with bleep-era minimalism. The closer, “Cosmic Ride”, is exactly that: a journey through spacey chords, dusty rhythm boxes, and that unmistakable feeling of warehouse euphoria at 4 a.m. Neutralise EP is a raw, timeless record that strips dance music down to its essence—jacking, emotional, physical. To match the sonic purity and timeless aesthetic of the release, we enlisted the iconic H5 studio—a name synonymous with visionary design in music and culture. Known for their groundbreaking work with Daft Punk, YSL, and numerous award-winning visual campaigns, H5 brings a level of artistic sophistication that elevates this EP into a complete sensory object. Their clean, modernist design echoes the stripped yet futuristic vibe of Tom Carruthers’ sound—a perfect fusion of form and function, underground and high art. Vinyl only. No digital. No compromise. For fans of: Virgo Four, Baby Ford, Larry Heard, early Warp, Mr. Fingers, and Beppe Loda.

Tracklist:

  • A1.Neutralise
  • A2.Deep north
  • A3.No More
  • B1.Pascals
  • B2.Cosmic ride

Originally released back in 2000, the music has lost none of its freshness, brimming with raw funk and Motor City swagger. Blending cavalier sampling and agile instrumentation, the music darts through disco-infused hedonism, spoken-word mantras and blasts of soulful euphoria. Standouts are the timeless 'Don't You Want My Love', the gospel depth of 'The Thief That Stole My Sad Days', and the powerfully evocative title track. Must own, simple as that.

item.title: Alton Miller - Spirit Chaser
item.description: Label: Quintessentials | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: House , Deep House
item.content:encoded:
Label: Quintessentials

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: House , Deep House

Is there a more under-celebrated producer in deep house than Alton Miller? The Detroiter has been serving up sublime slabs of classy dancefloor deepness for decades (he made is debut way back in 1993) and has recorded for all manner of inspired imprints, but for one reason or another his work has not been celebrated as much as many of his peers. As this Quintessentials outing shows, Miller remains a master of his craft. Side A is all about 'Last One First', a lightly spacey slab of richly electronic Motor City deep house futurism that comes accompanied by the breezier, warmer and lighter 'Life Recorder remix'. In contrast, 'Give It Up' is gentler, sunnier and effortlessly soulful, with Shaka successfully re-framing it as a lightly Latin-tinged slab of soulful house jazziness.

Working as an ongoing lab for stripped percussion, rolling subs and mischievous loop science, this latching batch folds neatly into that joint approach, despite it being nearly 20 years running: aside from the title track, 'Loop Of Life' and 'Attendre Mon Coeur' ease out that familiar Mountain groove, deceptively simple on the surface yet built with the microscopic shifts they've honed over the years. For the first release on his self-titled imprint, New Jersey great Kerri Chandler has gone back to the future. The four tracks on show were all inspired by a particular period of his own musical heritage between the late 90s and late 2000s, when he released a number of much-loved EPs on NYC's Downtown 161 imprint. It's basically Chandler in colourful, warming and soulful hybrid garage-house/deep house mode. For proof, check the swinging and melody rich opener 'Mommy, What's a Record' and he thickset, early morning at the Shelter vibes of 'Downtown'. Elsewhere, 'Moving In' sees him pepper a slick, dreamy and kaleidoscopic groove with his own mesmerising piano improvisations, while 'The Phone Call' sees him wrap spacey synth solos around a typically infectious, stab-rich house groove.

If you ask us, Abacus doesn't quite get the props he deserves. He's a key architect of the deep house sound that emerged from Chicago in the 90s and some of his jams are amongst the best the genre ever produced. First released in 1994 on Prescription Records, this EP is a quiet masterpiece. Austin Bascom delivered four tracks that favoured mood, space and emotional weight over fleeting trends. Warm, enveloping chords sit alongside scorched sub-bass and subtly futuristic textures at a time when house was splintering toward the mainstream. 'The Relics EP' remained resolutely underground, however, and earned cult status among DJs and dancers alike.

This Ep will often fetch three figures on second-hand markets and is one of many classics for the fawned-over Driftwood label. 'Luxury' and 'Milestones' glide with signature understated elegance, while 'Coming Over To You' balances intimacy and groove with effortless poise. Closer 'Deepness Is Served' lives up to its name, a masterclass in layered textures, rich basslines and warm melodic accents. At once sexy, considered and timeless.

Some classically timeless, retro-futurist deep house warmth here, as Pisa producer Niccolo Turini makes his bow on Gert-Jan Bijl aka Gerd's long-running 4 Lux label. Rich in classic drum and synth-sounds, much of the material is propulsive and energetic enough for peak-time floors, but thanks to its atmospheric sonics and huggable motifs could also be played in warm-up or after-hours sets. Highlights include Mr Fingers-influenced early morning deep house jazziness of 'Let The Music Bring You Up', the chunky and wide-eyed 'Take Me To The Moon', the weighty deep-and-jacking headiness of 'People From My Loves' and the simply gorgeous 'Get Down'

item.title: Infra Red - Metamorphasis (Reissue)
item.description: Label: Back To Life | Prix: 18,00 € | Style: 90 House , Techno
item.content:encoded:
Label: Back To Life

Prix: 18,00 €

Style: 90 House , Techno

Back To Life resurrects a key frame in Canadian house with a refresher reissue of 'Metamorphasis', the 1991 debut 12" on Ron Allen and Hayden Andre's Strobe Records and the first outing for their joint alias Infra-Red. Allen, a Toronto producer who soni-coined a jazz-aware strain of deep house on his own Phuture Funk imprint; and Andre, known for his crystalline piano work and precise drum programming; sketched out a six-track set full of thrustered jets and sonic booming synth plumes, and which still feels forward to this day. The Hayden Andre mix of 'Metamorphasis' bathes its chords in gauzy warmth, while the R2R take stiffens the pulse. 'Spectre' nods toward bleep, and 'Falling From The Light' appears in two contrasting versions, before 'Calibrate This' closes with much cooler machine poise.
